external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the SaaS portal and pushes a nightly supplier data extract.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload compliance paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: A service in the cloud account that loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor's platform where supplier compliance documents remain.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organization's cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a landing bucket in our cloud account
data_stores.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: The database in the organization's cloud account into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: Supplier compliance paperwork, including insurance certificates, food safety audits, and staff contact details, is uploaded to the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for suppliers' staff

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A supplier signs in to the portal using credentials issued by the vendor.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: review and approve
data_flows.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it through the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded compliance paperwork and approval or rejection decisions

data_flows.name: store documents
data_flows.description: The portal stores uploaded supplier documents in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_flows.name: retrieve documents
data_flows.description: The portal retrieves uploaded documents from the vendor platform for review.

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: The source says the extract is encrypted end to end, while the runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_flows.name: load extract
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the nightly extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database
data_flows.data_description: Supplier records from the nightly extract

trust_boundaries.name: vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled hosting zone containing the SaaS portal and vendor platform.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organization's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier is modeled as a human external entity because suppliers sign in and upload paperwork.
assumptions.basis: The text says suppliers sign in with a username and password and upload paperwork through the portal.

assumptions.assumption: The category manager is modeled as a human external entity because category managers review and approve or reject paperwork.
assumptions.basis: The text describes category managers as people who work from the corporate network and review submissions.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier document portal presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The component is explicitly described as a portal through which suppliers upload documents and category managers review them.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier platform and database contents are confidential because they contain compliance records and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The platform stores insurance certificates, food safety audits, and staff contact details.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket contents are confidential because it receives the supplier data extract.
assumptions.basis: The bucket receives a supplier data extract containing supplier records.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database contents are confidential because it stores supplier records derived from the extract.
